name: HIPAA Security Rule & Breach Notification
authority: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
description: 45 CFR Part 164 Subparts C (Security) and D (Breach Notification), as amended by the HITECH Act and the 2013 Omnibus Rule. Obligation is modelled per the rule's own required/addressable distinction. NOTE: 'addressable' does NOT mean optional - it means implement it, or document a reasoned assessment of why it is not reasonable and appropriate and what equivalent measure was adopted instead. An undocumented addressable specification is a finding.

sections.title: Subpart C — Security Standards for the Protection of ePHI
Subpart D — Notification in the Case of Breach of Unsecured PHI

requirements.title: Security management process
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain and correct security violations.

requirements.title: Risk analysis
requirements.text: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of ePHI held by the entity.
requirements.guidance: This is the single most-cited deficiency in OCR enforcement actions. It must be organization-wide, documented, and periodically refreshed - a vulnerability scan is not a risk analysis.

requirements.title: Risk management
requirements.text: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.

requirements.title: Sanction policy
requirements.text: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the entity.

requirements.title: Information system activity review
requirements.text: Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports and security incident tracking reports.

requirements.title: Assigned security responsibility
requirements.text: Identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by this subpart.

requirements.title: Workforce security
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to ensure that all workforce members have appropriate access to ePHI, and to prevent those who should not have access from obtaining it.

requirements.title: Authorization and/or supervision
requirements.text: Implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with ePHI or in locations where it might be accessed.

requirements.title: Workforce clearance procedure
requirements.text: Implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to ePHI is appropriate.

requirements.title: Termination procedures
requirements.text: Implement procedures for terminating access to ePHI when employment ends or when access is no longer appropriate.

requirements.title: Information access management
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to ePHI consistent with the applicable requirements of Subpart E.

requirements.title: Isolating health care clearinghouse functions
requirements.text: If a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, implement policies and procedures to protect ePHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization.

requirements.title: Access authorization
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures for granting access to ePHI, for example through access to a workstation, transaction, program or process.

requirements.title: Access establishment and modification
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures that, based upon the entity's access authorization policies, establish, document, review and modify a user's right of access.

requirements.title: Security awareness and training
requirements.text: Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of the workforce, including management.

requirements.title: Security reminders
requirements.text: Provide periodic security updates to the workforce.

requirements.title: Protection from malicious software
requirements.text: Implement procedures for guarding against, detecting and reporting malicious software.

requirements.title: Log-in monitoring
requirements.text: Implement procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.

requirements.title: Password management
requirements.text: Implement procedures for creating, changing and safeguarding passwords.

requirements.title: Security incident procedures
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents.

requirements.title: Response and reporting
requirements.text: Identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate, to the extent practicable, their harmful effects; and document the incidents and their outcomes.

requirements.title: Contingency plan
requirements.text: Establish policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence that damages systems containing ePHI.

requirements.title: Data backup plan
requirements.text: Establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of ePHI.

requirements.title: Disaster recovery plan
requirements.text: Establish and implement procedures to restore any loss of data.

requirements.title: Emergency mode operation plan
requirements.text: Establish and implement procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of ePHI while operating in emergency mode.

requirements.title: Testing and revision procedures
requirements.text: Implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.

requirements.title: Applications and data criticality analysis
requirements.text: Assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components.

requirements.title: Evaluation
requirements.text: Perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation of the extent to which security policies and procedures meet the requirements of this subpart, in response to environmental or operational changes.

requirements.title: Business associate contracts and other arrangements
requirements.text: A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain or transmit ePHI on its behalf only if it obtains satisfactory assurances, documented in a written contract, that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information.

requirements.title: Facility access controls
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring that properly authorized access is allowed.

requirements.title: Contingency operations
requirements.text: Establish procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery and emergency mode operations plans.

requirements.title: Facility security plan
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering and theft.

requirements.title: Access control and validation procedures
requirements.text: Implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control and control of access to software programs for testing and revision.

requirements.title: Maintenance records
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility which are related to security.

requirements.title: Workstation use
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner of performance, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access ePHI.

requirements.title: Workstation security
requirements.text: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access ePHI to restrict access to authorized users.

requirements.title: Device and media controls
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing ePHI into and out of a facility, and their movement within the facility.

requirements.title: Disposal
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of ePHI, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored.

requirements.title: Media re-use
requirements.text: Implement procedures for removal of ePHI from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.

requirements.title: Accountability
requirements.text: Maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefore.

requirements.title: Data backup and storage
requirements.text: Create a retrievable, exact copy of ePHI, when needed, before movement of equipment.

requirements.title: Access control
requirements.text: Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain ePHI to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights.

requirements.title: Unique user identification
requirements.text: Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
requirements.guidance: Shared or generic administrative accounts defeat this outright, and also make 164.312(b) audit controls unattributable.

requirements.title: Emergency access procedure
requirements.text: Establish and implement procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.

requirements.title: Automatic logoff
requirements.text: Implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.

requirements.title: Encryption and decryption
requirements.text: Implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI.
requirements.guidance: Addressable, but encryption meeting HHS guidance is also the safe harbour in the Breach Notification Rule: encrypted data rendered unusable is not 'unsecured PHI', so a loss may not be a reportable breach at all.

requirements.title: Audit controls
requirements.text: Implement hardware, software and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use ePHI.

requirements.title: Integrity
requirements.text: Implement policies and procedures to protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction.

requirements.title: Mechanism to authenticate ePHI
requirements.text: Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.

requirements.title: Person or entity authentication
requirements.text: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.

requirements.title: Transmission security
requirements.text: Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI being transmitted over an electronic communications network.

requirements.title: Integrity controls
requirements.text: Implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.

requirements.title: Encryption (transmission)
requirements.text: Implement a mechanism to encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate.

requirements.title: Business associate contracts or other arrangements
requirements.text: The contract or other arrangement must provide that the business associate will comply with the Security Rule, ensure that subcontractors who create, receive, maintain or transmit ePHI agree to the same restrictions, and report security incidents including breaches of unsecured PHI.

requirements.title: Requirements for group health plans
requirements.text: A group health plan must ensure its plan documents require the sponsor to reasonably and appropriately safeguard ePHI it creates, receives, maintains or transmits on behalf of the plan.

requirements.title: Policies and procedures
requirements.text: Implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards and implementation specifications of this subpart, and change them as needed.

requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.text: Maintain the policies and procedures in written form, and where an action, activity or assessment is required to be documented, maintain a written record of it.

requirements.title: Documentation — time limit
requirements.text: Retain documentation for six years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.

requirements.title: Documentation — availability
requirements.text: Make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

requirements.title: Documentation — updates
requirements.text: Review documentation periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of ePHI.

requirements.title: Notification to individuals
requirements.text: Following discovery of a breach of unsecured PHI, notify each affected individual without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery, including the required content elements.

requirements.title: Notification to the media
requirements.text: For a breach involving more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction, notify prominent media outlets serving that State or jurisdiction without unreasonable delay and within 60 calendar days.

requirements.title: Notification to the Secretary
requirements.text: Notify HHS of breaches: contemporaneously with individual notice for breaches of 500 or more individuals; annually within 60 days of the end of the calendar year for smaller breaches.

requirements.title: Notification by a business associate
requirements.text: A business associate must notify the covered entity of a breach of unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery, identifying each affected individual to the extent possible.
requirements.guidance: This is the operative obligation for a technology vendor acting as a Business Associate. The clock starts at discovery, and discovery is imputed when any workforce member or agent knew or should have known.

requirements.title: Law enforcement delay
requirements.text: Delay notification where a law enforcement official states that notification would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security, for the period specified in a written statement or 30 days for an oral statement.

requirements.title: Administrative requirements and burden of proof
requirements.text: Comply with the applicable administrative requirements of 164.530, and maintain the burden of demonstrating that all required notifications were made or that an impermissible use or disclosure did not constitute a breach, including a documented four-factor risk assessment.
